in_arabic.name: إِشَام
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم إِشَام مشتق من الجذر العربي 'ش-أ-م' الذي يحمل معاني الإِعظام و التَعظيم. ورد ذكره في بعض الآثار النبوية و يستخدم في الثقافة الإسلامية لتعظيم و تكريم الشخص

in_urdu.name: اشام
in_urdu.meaning: اشام کا مطلب ہے عظمت و شان
in_urdu.long_meaning: اشام نام عربی جڑ 'ش-أ-م' سے ماخوذ ہے جس کے معنی عظمت و شان کے ہیں۔ یہ نام اسلامی ثقافت میں عظمت و احترام کے لئے استعمال کیا جاتا ہے، خاص طور پر جنوبی ایشیائی مسلمانوں میں

in_hindi.name: इशाम
in_hindi.meaning: इशाम का अर्थ है महानता और सम्मान
in_hindi.long_meaning: इशाम नाम अरबी मूल 'श-आ-म' से लिया गया है जिसका अर्थ महानता और सम्मान है। यह नाम भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में एक महत्वपूर्ण और सम्मानजनक नाम के रूप में प्रयोग किया जाता है

in_pashto.name: اشام
in_pashto.meaning: اشام د لويه او درناوي معنی ورکوي
in_pashto.long_meaning: اشام نوم د عربي کلمو 'ش-أ-م' څخه اخیستل شوی دی چې د لويه او درناوي معنا لري. دا نوم د افغان او پښتن مسلمانو په کلتور کې د درناوي او لويه لپاره کارول کېږي

data.cultural_impact: The name "Ishaam" in Arabic language has its roots in the rich cultural tradition of the Islamic world. It is derived from the Arabic word "al-Hayy" which means "the Living One," or "The Ever-Living." Historically, this name was revered in the Arabian Peninsula, and it was often given to children as a reminder of the Almighty Allah's unending and eternal nature.
data.spiritual_significance: In a spiritual sense, the name "Ishaam" serves as a significant reminder of our connection to the Divine. It is a reminder of the belief in Allah's eternal existence and the importance of striving to live a life that is guided by His will and mercy. For those who bear this name, it is a constant reminder of their utmost respect and reverence for Allah, the giver of life and the sustainer of the universe. In essence, "Ishaam" symbolizes a deep and abiding faith in the Almighty, trusting Him for all the sustenance and success in life.

historical_references.reference: Ishaam ibn Amr as-Sakuni, a companion of the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh). He was known for his generosity and was given the nickname 'Ibn Al-Sadaqah' (Son of Alms). Ishaam was one of the ten companions of the Prophet (pbuh) who were given the title 'Ashareh Mubashsharun' (The Ten Promised Paradise). He was also one of the forty men who were given the title 'Sawad Al-Asharah' (The Forty Righteous Men). Ishaam participated in various battles, including the Battle of Uhud, and was also a scribe and a teacher. He died around 55 AH/674 CE.
historical_references.context: Islamic history, Companions of the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh)

historical_references.reference: Ishaam ibn Ali, the fifth Iman (leader) of the Shia Muslims. He ruled from 762 to 773 AH/1360 to 1371 CE. Ishaam faced many challenges during his rule, including rebellions from various provinces and conflicts with the Abbasid Caliphate. He is known for his efforts to promote peace and justice, and for his generosity towards his people. Ishaam also established the city of Samarra as a new capital for the Abbasid Caliphate, which became an important cultural and religious center for the Shia Muslims. He died in 773 AH/1372 CE.
